answer: Cross-epoch behaviour fingerprinting. Each identity must keep a stable behavioural signature — response latency, task mix, error profile — across epochs; drift beyond a tolerance flags it. Like an ocean current, continuity is measured, not assumed. An attacker splitting into many identities must maintain each separately, paying per-identity the cost of coherent, non-repeating activity. A single dune of deviation exposes the farm. Residual ember: each fake identity still needs sustained, distinct behaviour, multiplying effort linearly with sybil count.
